details.body: In `engine.rs:491`, the pre-step `enforce_invariants(&mut self.state)?` both clamps fields (e.g. `condition_index`, `ph`) and returns hard errors (e.g. for negative `reserve_g`). If the state has multiple issues, fields clamped before the first hard error remain silently modified even though the function returns `Err`. The validation tests in `validation.rs` (lines 90-123) assert `engine.full_state() == expected` after a failed `step_hours`, which only passes because each test injects exactly one bad field into an otherwise well-formed `TankState::new`. Consider splitting `enforce_invariants` into a read-only validation pass (for the pre-step guard) and a separate clamp-and-validate pass (for the post-step cleanup), or at minimum document the partial-mutation behavior and adjust the tests to tolerate it.

The `reserve_g` pool in `animal` accumulates from the `growth_fraction_of_assimilated` pathway (shrimp.rs:234) but is only drained by shrimp mortality (shrimp.rs:601-606). No metabolic baseline drain, molt cost, or reproductive cost draws from `reserve_g`. With default parameters (10 adults, ae=0.5, growth_frac=0.2), reserve accumulates ~0.001 g/day and exceeds total shrimp body mass (~1.2g) within a few simulated years. The `total_nitrogen` / `total_carbon` accounting (budget.rs:247-248, 332-333) correctly tracks this pool, so mass is conserved, but the unbounded accumulation is biologically implausible and may confuse diagnostic outputs. Add a code comment in `route_consumed_food` noting that `reserve_g` will grow without bound in phase 1 and that a metabolic maintenance drain is expected in the reserve/condition bead (tanksim-6e5.6.1).

The invariant `check_unit_interval` for `shrimp_assimilation_efficiency` (invariants.rs:186-188) accepts the boundary values 0.0 and 1.0. With `ae = 0.0`, all food becomes feces and nothing is assimilated (no TAN, no DIC, no O2 demand, no reserve growth). With `ae = 1.0`, no feces are produced at all. Both are physically degenerate. The doc comment on the field says 'Literature range: 0.4–0.7' (process.rs:187). Consider using a strict open-interval check `(0.0 < ae < 1.0)` or at minimum `check_positive` to reject exactly-zero, matching the intent expressed by the test `default_fraction_sums_are_valid` (shrimp_feeding_pathway.rs:81) which asserts `ae > 0.0 && ae < 1.0`.

Use a consistent mass basis for shrimp ingestion/routing. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:153-166` records consumed food in grams, but `route_consumed_food` (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:183-235`) only partitions the elemental N+C returned by `algae_nitrogen_mg`/`algae_carbon_mg` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:371-376`). For periphyton, 1 g consumed becomes only 35 mg N + 218.75 mg C = 0.25375 g routed back into feces/reserve/respiration/excretion, so most of the consumed gram mass still disappears relative to `daily_food_consumed_g`. That misses the bead’s “assimilated plus fecal mass equals consumed mass” contract and makes satiation/condition run on a different basis than the routed matter budget.

Wire the new shrimp routing coefficients through the preset/materialization path instead of silently discarding them. `crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:85-94` defines `shrimp_assimilation_efficiency`, the assimilated partition fractions, and `shrimp_o2_per_mg_c_respired`, but `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:191-335` has no matching `ProcessParamsPreset` fields and `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:427-435` still fills `ProcessParams` from `ProcessParams::default()`. As shipped, tuning those TOML values has no effect and bad preset values are ignored instead of validated, so the new named controls are not actually data-backed.

BUG: In `engine.rs` RemoveShrimp handler (line 404), the reserve fraction denominator uses only `self.state.animal.adults_count` instead of `adults_count + juveniles_count`. When juveniles exist, removing all adults drains 100% of the shared reserve (fraction = count/adults_count = 1.0), leaving surviving juveniles with zero reserve. The parallel code in `route_dead_shrimp_to_detritus` (shrimp.rs:598) correctly uses `state.animal.adults_count + state.animal.juveniles_count` as the denominator. Fix: change line 404 from `let total = self.state.animal.adults_count;` to `let total = self.state.animal.adults_count + self.state.animal.juveniles_count;`.

Correctness gap: In `route_consumed_food` (shrimp.rs:224-225), the O2 consumption is clamped at zero via `.max(0.0)`, but the carbon and nitrogen routing (respired_c → DIC, respired_n → TAN) proceeds at full rate regardless of actual O2 availability. This breaks the stoichiometric coupling: when DO is exhausted, the model produces DIC and TAN as if aerobic respiration occurred, but no O2 was actually consumed. Consider either (a) scaling respired_c_mg and respired_n_mg by `actual_o2_consumed / o2_demand_mg` when O2 is limiting, or (b) adding a brief code comment explicitly acknowledging this as a Phase 1 simplification so downstream C7/C4 audits don't need to rediscover it.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:446-451`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:532-538`, and especially `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:631-670` let hatching and juvenile maturation fund new shrimp biomass from `DON/TAN` and `DOC/DIC` whenever `animal.reserve_g` is short. That bypasses the new ingestion -> assimilation -> retained-reserve pathway and allows shrimp biomass to be created from dissolved waste/carbonate pools instead of only from retained intake. Reproduction/growth should stay limited by reserve (or explicitly fail/stall) rather than mining water-column dissolved pools.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:78-86` runs `shrimp_feeding()` before `update_condition()`, but the carbonate cache is not refreshed until `refresh_carbonate_state()` at the end of the daily step. `route_consumed_food()` mutates TAN/DIC/DO in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:211-229`, and `update_condition()` immediately recomputes NH3 using `state.water.ph` in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:243-245`. Same-day condition/reproduction logic therefore uses stale pre-feeding pH instead of the post-feeding carbonate state. Refresh carbonate state immediately after feeding (or inside the routing helper) before any pH-dependent calculations.

The v3→v4 save migration for `reserve_g` should seed the reserve proportionally to the existing shrimp population instead of defaulting to 0.0. When an old save with an established colony (e.g. 30 adults, 20 juveniles) is loaded, `reserve_g = 0.0` causes all hatching (`fund_hatched_clutch_biomass`) and juvenile maturation (`fund_live_shrimp_biomass`) to fail until enough feeding cycles accumulate reserve. The migration function `migrate_v3_to_v4` should compute a reasonable initial reserve — e.g. `reserve_g = shrimp_biomass_g(adults, juveniles) * LIVE_BIOMASS_ORGANIC_FRACTION_G_PER_G` — so established populations don't experience a transient reproduction/growth block on upgrade.

Add an alkalinity adjustment when TAN is produced by shrimp excretion and respiration in `route_consumed_food`. When amino acids are catabolized, each mole of NH3/NH4+ released increases alkalinity by approximately 1 meq. The current code adds TAN to `ammonia_total_mg_n_total` but does not adjust `alkalinity_meq_total`. At the excretion+respiration rates in this model (excr_frac=0.10, resp_frac=0.70 of assimilated N), omitting this coupling will cause pH to drift lower than it should over time because the DIC increase from respiration suppresses pH without the counterbalancing alkalinity increase from ammonia release. Add: `state.water.alkalinity_meq_total += (excreted_n_mg + respired_n_mg) / 14.007` (converting mg N to meq NH3).

In `shrimp_feeding` (shrimp.rs:140-153), periphyton demand and detritus demand are computed independently at the full feeding rate, allowing shrimp to consume up to 2x the parameterized `shrimp_periphyton_grazing_g_per_shrimp_per_day` when both food sources are plentiful. This is undocumented and may cause unexpectedly high bioload. Add a comment explaining this is intentional opportunistic feeding, OR split the demand so total intake is bounded by the rate parameter (e.g., remaining demand after periphyton goes to detritus).

Restore a compatibility migration for missing `animal.reserve_g` in schema-3 saves. `migrate_v3_to_v4` is now a no-op (`crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:323-329`), so legacy colonies load with `reserve_g = 0`. That breaks save-upgrade continuity because hatching and juvenile maturation now hard-require reserve (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:461-468`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:646-651`); a v3 save with berried females or near-mature juveniles will stall or fail immediately after upgrade until the colony re-feeds. The changed expectation in `crates/tank_core/tests/save_load.rs:274-320` is codifying that regression. Reconstruct reserve from legacy shrimp state, or at least seed enough reserve to honor already-serialized egg/maturation commitments.
